prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (ideological framing removed)

Economy and tax
- Reduce employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish the main rate of self-employed NI by the end of the Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT rates.
- Maintain the National Living Wage at two-thirds of median earnings.
- Triple Lock Plus for pensioners: uprate both State Pension and a new age-related personal allowance by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%; maintain existing pensioner benefits.
- Raise at least £6 billion a year by tackling tax avoidance/evasion.

Business, regulation and government efficiency
- Keep corporation tax rate; consider extending full expensing to leasing when affordable.
- Ten-point SME plan (business rates support, VAT threshold smoothing, prompt payment enforcement, better finance access, Invest in Women Fund, more SME-friendly procurement).
- Public R&D to £22bn a year; invest in AI compute; £4.5bn for advanced manufacturing; retain R&D tax reliefs; strengthen financial services competitiveness.
- Continue post‑EU regulatory reform; cut civil service to pre‑pandemic size; halve consultant spend; move 25,000 roles out of London; target 2% annual public-sector productivity growth.

Infrastructure and transport
- Reallocate £36bn HS2 savings to regional roads, rail and buses; major schemes incl. parts of Northern Powerhouse Rail, Midlands Rail Hub, electrify North Wales Main Line; station accessibility upgrades.
- Expand EV charging; support sustainable aviation fuels; maritime review.
- Speed up planning for major projects.
- Rail Reform Bill to create Great British Railways; extend £2 bus fare cap.
- Backing Drivers Bill: ban road pricing by local authorities, reverse the London ULEZ expansion, require local referendums for new 20mph zones and Low Traffic Neighbourhoods; roll out National Parking Platform; no new smart motorways.

Families, education and skills
- 30 hours free childcare from 9 months to school start by Sept 2025; nationwide Family Hubs.
- Child Benefit moved to a household test with higher thresholds.
- Ban mobile phones during the school day; parents’ right to see teaching materials.
- Advanced British Standard (merge A levels/T levels); 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by curbing low‑outcome degree places; Lifelong Learning Entitlement.
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (paid competitive military postings or civic service).

Welfare and work
- Reform disability benefits and work capability assessments; overhaul fit notes via specialist assessors; tougher sanctions after 12 months; complete Universal Credit rollout; new Fraud Bill; strengthen Child Maintenance Service.

Health and social care
- Real-terms NHS budget growth; expand workforce (+92,000 nurses, +28,000 doctors), Pharmacy First, 250 GP surgeries, 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.
- Dental Recovery Plan, including service commitment for new dentists.
- £3.4bn for NHS tech (NHS App as single front door, AI diagnostics, Federated Data Platform); reduce managers by 5,500.
- Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco & Vapes Bill; women’s health measures; implement Cass Review; expand mental health support; infected blood compensation scheme.

Security, defence and foreign policy
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; invest in munitions and defence innovation; veterans’ legislation and benefits; National Defence and Resilience Plan; continued support for Ukraine; strengthen foreign influence rules; development spending to return to 0.7% of GNI when fiscal conditions allow.

Borders and immigration
- Binding annual legal cap on work/family visas that falls each year, set by Parliament; higher salary thresholds; limits on dependants; health checks and higher surcharges/fees.
- Monthly removals to Rwanda; implement Illegal Migration Act; pursue asylum treaty reforms and returns deals; capped safe/legal routes set by Parliament based on local capacity.

Energy and climate
- Net zero 2050; annual North Sea licensing; maintain windfall tax to 2028–29; new gas plants as backup.
- Treble offshore wind; launch carbon capture clusters; expand nuclear (approve two SMR fleets; progress Wylfa); Green Industries Growth Accelerator.
- Lower green levies; energy-efficiency vouchers and funding; review standing charges; PumpWatch; onshore wind with local consent; rooftop/brownfield solar; retain fracking moratorium.

Housing and communities
- 1.6m homes; fast-track brownfield, higher urban densities, urban development corporations; mitigate nutrient neutrality via fees; support small builders; protect Green Belt.
- Make permanent the £425k first-time buyer Stamp Duty threshold; new Help to Buy; extend Mortgage Guarantee.
- Renters Reform Bill (end Section 21 alongside court changes); complete leasehold reform; rough sleeping plan; regulate holiday lets.
- Town endowment funds; extend Shared Prosperity Fund; expand Freeports and Investment Zones.

Farming, fisheries, rural and environment
- Increase UK-wide farming budget by £1bn over the Parliament; legal food security target and index; at least 50% of public food spend local/higher standard; faster farm infrastructure planning; tapered seasonal worker scheme; renew £100m Seafood Fund.
- Maintain elevated flood defence funding.
- Plan for Water: tougher enforcement, river restoration network, regulatory reform.
- Tree/peat programmes; designate a new National Park; deposit return scheme; tougher fly-tipping penalties; limit new waste incinerators.

Union and devolution
- Protect the UK internal market; UK‑wide comparable performance data; continued direct investment across Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; implement Windsor Framework and legacy processes.
